question: Will Donald Trump publicly insult Tucker Carlson by July 31, 2026?
rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump makes any public statement in which he insults, mocks, or attacks the listed individual personally or professionally in a clearly negative manner between market creation and the specified date (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

This includes calling the individual weak, stupid, disloyal, a failure, using an insulting nickname, using other derogatory language, or using the negative form of a positive trait in a derogatory personal way (e.g., “He/She isn’t smart”). Negative forms used in reference to the individual's professional actions, policies, or decisions (e.g., “He/She isn’t being smart about this policy”) will not count. Policy disagreements stated without disparaging language will not count.

A direct reference will qualify even if the individual is not named, so long as it is reasonably clear from context that they are the subject.

Any written, verbal, or recorded public statement by Trump qualifies.

The resolution source for this market will be public statements from Donald Trump.

evidence.excerpt: Tucker Carlson branded President Donald Trump a “weak” man who allowed Israel to strong-arm him into the Iran war. The remarks came during a July 15 interview on Bloomberg journalist Mishal Husain’s podcast. Carlson said, “I have held him directly accountable, it’s his fault, he’s the U.S. president, he was elected.”

Carlson said he had not spoken to Trump since the regime-change war began and added, “I’m not interested in talking to him.” He said, “I’m going to help build a third party,” while also stating that he was not a politician or a rival to Trump for power.

Carlson told Sky News interviewer Yalda Hakim that his last conversation with Trump was February 27, before the Iran war began. In a separate interview with Jack Neel, Carlson mocked Trump’s posture toward Iran and said, “Shut up, b*tch! I don’t take you seriously.” The article also reported that Trump had called Carlson a “low-IQ person” and “highly overrated” in a Truth Social post.

Carlson said on the podcast “Can’t Be Censored” that “there’s no chance I would support the Republican Party” ahead of the November midterm elections. He also said he would not support the Democratic Party. The Associated Press reported that his estrangement from Republicans had intensified after Trump’s decision to go to war with Iran.

evidence.excerpt: Trump wrote, “It’s easy! Tucker is a Low IQ person - Always easy to beat, and highly overrated!!!” The April 17 Truth Social compilation records the statement at 5:12 a.m. Pacific time.

evidence.excerpt: Trump opened a Truth Social post with, “Who’s dumber, Tucker Carlson or Joe Kent?” He later wrote, “Kent is a LOSER, just like Tucker, Candace, Megyn, and the rest of them are LOSERS,” and described them as “LOW IQ.” The compilation records the post at 3:08 p.m. Pacific time on April 16.

ABC News reported that Trump posted a lengthy critique of Tucker Carlson, Megyn Kelly, Candace Owens and Alex Jones on Truth Social. Trump said they had “one thing in common, Low IQs” and wrote, “They’re not ‘MAGA,’ they’re losers.” The article was published April 9, 2026, at 9:42 p.m. ET.
